title: Brand ink · roller run-out

reference.grammar: The drawdown card's roller on its own: every control changes the roll and nothing else. The spec card for a grocer's one brand color, rolled once across the card over white and over a black opacity band. Set the paper, how much ink the roller carries and how fast it gives out, how hard the hand leans and drifts, what the roller is made of, and how the ink splits. The five stations are recomputed from the same film model on every change. The brand ink is in the Color tab. The type is printed as AP-36 opens and does not move.

techniques.name: Paper

paper.label: Paper
paper.note: coated: fine, even speckle; bond: fibrous; cold press: coarse tooth and deep valleys

techniques.implementation: The sheet is FX-03 live: tooth, formation, fibers and pits under the one sheet light. As the ink gives out it only reaches the paper's peaks, so the run-out speckle is the paper itself: fine and even on coated board, fibrous on bond, coarse and deep on cold press.
techniques.limits: One sheet: the paper under the type changes with it.

techniques.name: Roller

load.label: Ink on the roller
load.note: how far along the stroke the roller is down to half its ink. More ink, a longer solid

runout.label: Run-out
runout.note: how much of the stroke the ink takes to give out: a short burst or a long fade

pressure.label: Pressure
pressure.note: how hard the hand leans. Below 1 the solid opens onto the paper before the ink runs out

drift.label: Hand drift
drift.note: the hand turns off square: the run-out line and the streaks tilt with it

roller.label: Roller
roller.note: hard rubber: crisp ends and a ridge of squeezed ink; soft rubber: a softer edge; foam: a wandering edge and an open, cellular film

seed.label: Pass
seed.note: roll it again: the same settings, a new pass

techniques.implementation: One pass of a hand roller. Ink on the roller sets where along the stroke it is down to half its ink, Run-out how much of the stroke that takes, Pressure how hard the hand leans (below 1 the solid opens onto the paper before the ink runs out), Hand drift how far the run-out line turns off square. The roller sets its ends and wander: hard rubber prints crisp ends with a ridge of squeezed ink that holds into the run-out, soft rubber a softer edge, foam a wandering edge and an open, cellular film.
techniques.limits: Run-out under 6% is a hard vector edge. Hand drift past 15° turns the run-out off the strip before the stations can read it.

techniques.name: Ink

body.label: Ink body
body.note: 0 loose: a thin film that fades to tone. 1 stiff: a tacky ink that breaks into sharp specks at full strength

clump.label: Clump size
clump.note: how big the film's own breaks are as it splits off the roller

streak.label: Streak
streak.note: clumps drawn out along the stroke: a dry roller, a fast pass

techniques.implementation: The ink as it splits between roller and paper (the ink chain): the paper's height, blended with the film's own split, is ranked so that pressure P inks exactly the top P of the surface. A stiff ink breaks into sharp specks at full strength; a loose one stays a thinner, whole film that fades. Clump size is how big the film's own breaks are; Streak draws them out along the stroke. The color is the Color tab.
techniques.limits: Clump size past 2.5 px reads as blotches. Streak past 6 reads as scanlines.

pass_order: Paper · the sheet the roller meets: coated, bond or cold press.
Roller · how much ink it carries, how fast it gives out, how hard the hand leans and drifts, and what the roller is made of.
Ink · how the film splits onto the paper's peaks; its color is the Color tab.
